notes: NWC construction: NWC = (Total current assets - Cash and cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - Short-term borrowings and current portion of long-term debt). This excludes debt-bearing current liabilities and excludes cash. Component values taken from Labcorp balance sheets. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
Historical 'ebit' is modeled as Operating income from Labcorp consolidated statements of operations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Historical 'da' is modeled as Depreciation and amortization from the consolidated statement of cash flows (includes depreciation/amortization items within cash flow). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Base-case forecast drivers are assumption-based (not consensus-derived) and are calibrated to FY2025 starting profitability, plus management-stated capex direction for 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
WACC is an estimated modeling input (not sourced) and may require adjustment to match the specific DCF pipeline's capital structure and risk parameters.

NOL balance: computed from disclosed U.S. federal/state and foreign tax loss carryforwards in the 10-K text; it is not a single consolidated 'NOL' line item and capital-loss carryforwards are not included as NOL. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Continued execution on organic volume and pricing momentum in Dx and BLS, leading to faster-than-modeled revenue growth. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Capex and facility investment progress (including LaunchPad-related spending referenced by management) that supports throughput and margin resilience. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
Leverage and capital allocation outcomes (cash generation and working capital timing) that change net debt/equity bridge dynamics.
company_overview: Labcorp reports two operating segments: Diagnostics Laboratories (Dx) and Biopharma Laboratory Services (BLS). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Dx provides routine testing and specialty/esoteric testing through a network of primary and specialty laboratories (primarily North America). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

BLS primarily serves pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and diagnostic companies and CROs through its central laboratory and ED businesses. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 revenue was $13.9517B (+7.2% vs. FY2024) and operating income was $1.3847B (+27.4% vs. FY2024), supporting the step-up in profitability assumed in the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Cash and cash equivalents declined to $532.3M at December 31, 2025 (from $1,518.7M at December 31, 2024), so enterprise valuation inputs materially matter for the equity value bridge. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Capital expenditures were $434.5M in FY2025 (3.1% of revenue) and management expected capex to rise to ~4.0% of revenues in 2026, which is reflected directly in the forecast capex intensity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
The effective tax rate for FY2025 was 20.7%, used as the base-case tax_rate input. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Revenue base-case assumes deceleration from the FY2025 growth rate to mid-single-digit levels, consistent with how management framed organic growth plus acquisition and FX contributions. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin base-case gradually steps up to ~10.6% by 2029-2030, anchored to the FY2025 operating margin level and then held relatively steady. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

D&A intensity is held near the FY2023-2025 average range to reflect ongoing depreciation/amortization from the existing asset base. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Capex intensity is set higher in 2026 (reflecting expected ~4.0% of revenue) and then normalized downward slightly to maintain economic sense in terminal years. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Working capital intensity is modeled at ~7-8% of sales (base-case), using a consistent NWC construction that excludes cash and excludes debt-bearing current liabilities. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920148/000092014825000032/lh-20241231.htm))
key_risks: Reimbursement/pricing pressure or demand variability could slow revenue growth and delay EBIT margin recovery from FY2025 levels.

Working capital volatility (especially in accounts receivable/unbilled services and payables timing) can create unfavorable FCF outcomes vs. the modeled NWC intensity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Tax and NOL utilization uncertainty: while NOL carryforwards exist, the modeled utilization percent may differ from realized outcomes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

Execution risk from acquisitions/integration and restructuring charges that can affect both margins and cash conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920148/000092014826000111/lh-20251231.htm))

presentation.subtitle: Labcorp (LH): DCF + Comps Inputs (FY2025 base year)
valuation_summary: Base-case forecasts chain from the last historical year (FY2025 revenue) using explicit revenue growth assumptions, and validation_support.forecast_revenue provides QA-ready absolute revenue levels for each forecast year.

Terminal value uses a Gordon Growth framework (gordon_growth), with terminal_growth set to 3.0% as a long-run steady-state proxy; comps are used primarily to sanity-check valuation breadth rather than to mechanically set terminal exit multiples.
